title: Local noetherian model for a section component
statement: For a locally finitely presented, quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism of schemes g : P ⟶ T with section σ, every point p has an open neighbourhood U and noetherian schemes P₀,T₀ with corresponding morphism, section, and projection ρ such that the section component locus on U is the inverse image under ρ of the noetherian section component locus. Locally finite presentation is used as in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation].

source.place: Stacks Project, Tag 055P first reduction using 01ZM and 055M

proof.text: Choose an affine open V about g(p), set U=g⁻¹(V) and f=g restricted to V. The square with U→P and V→T is cartesian. Its universal lift of V→T→P and the identity on V gives the restricted section σ_V; projection identities prove both section compatibility equations.

Apply [lem-sbc-affine-section-noetherian-descent] to f and σ_V. Obtain the noetherian source and base, finite-presentation model g₀, its section σ₀, and a cartesian comparison ρ from U, compatible with the sections.

Apply [lem-sbc-section-component-cartesian] once to the affine restriction square and once to the noetherian model square. The first equality identifies U.ι⁻¹ of the original locus with the restricted locus. The second identifies ρ⁻¹ of the model locus with that same restricted locus. Transitivity with the symmetry of the second equality proves the required equality.

proof_origin.note: R3: full Lean proof. The two geometric steps are proved in cycle-free supporting modules, using existing proved descent and geometric connectedness theorems.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_section_component_noetherian_model {P T : Scheme.{u}} (g : P ⟶ T)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation g] [QuasiCompact g] [QuasiSeparated g]
    (σ : T ⟶ P) (hσ : σ ≫ g = 𝟙 T) (p : P) :
    ∃ (U : P.Opens), p ∈ U ∧ ∃ (P₀ T₀ : Scheme.{u}) (g₀ : P₀ ⟶ T₀)
      (σ₀ : T₀ ⟶ P₀) (ρ : U.toScheme ⟶ P₀),
      IsNoetherian P₀ ∧ IsNoetherian T₀ ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation g₀ ∧
      QuasiCompact g₀ ∧ QuasiSeparated g₀ ∧ σ₀ ≫ g₀ = 𝟙 T₀ ∧
      U.ι ⁻¹' {q : P | q ∈ connectedComponentIn (g ⁻¹' {g q}) (σ (g q))} =
        ρ ⁻¹' {q : P₀ | q ∈ connectedComponentIn (g₀ ⁻¹' {g₀ q}) (σ₀ (g₀ q))}
